draft.title: Biotic and abiotic factors
card: a living part of an ecosystem, or something made by living things. Plants, animals, fungi and bacteria are biotic.
a non-living part of an ecosystem. Temperature, water, light, soil and wind are abiotic.
Both kinds affect how many of an organism can live in a place. A lack of water can shrink a plant population. More predators can shrink a prey population.
Biotic and abiotic factors also affect each other. Soil type, an abiotic factor, helps decide which plants grow, and those plants are biotic.
draft.remember: Living parts are biotic, non-living parts are abiotic, and both affect population sizes.

a.q: A desert ecosystem has many parts. Which one of them is abiotic?
a.why: Rainfall is a non-living part of the ecosystem, so it is abiotic. Bacteria are tempting because they are tiny and in the sand, but they are living things, so they are biotic.
a.clue: Which one is not alive and not made by living things?

b.q: A dry summer shrinks a pond in regional Victoria, and fewer frogs survive. Which statement about this is correct?
opts: Low water, an abiotic factor, cut a biotic population
The frogs, a biotic factor, caused the pond water to drop
One biotic factor shrank another biotic population here
Only living factors can change the size of a population
b.why: Water level is non-living, so it is abiotic, and it affected the number of frogs. Frogs are living, but they did not cause the drop in water. Abiotic factors can change populations as well as biotic ones.
b.clue: Decide whether water and frogs are living, then see which one caused the change.

b.best: Low water, an abiotic factor, cut a biotic population
